page.layout: One page of text, centred verse with acrostic letters in both margins. Running head top left, page number top right. Opening verse line at full width at the top. Below it: the author heading and acrostic poem (Kesler), with letters P E T R V S in the left margin and M A R T Y R in the right margin. Then the Haller poems, each with its heading, and the Greek and Latin title line. Signature at the lower right of the text block.

main_text.p: Illic cum Domino JESV licet esse beatis Semper, & aeterna vivere laetitia.
main_text.head: JOANNIS KESLERI Sangallensis.
main_text.p: Petro illi nomen, firmo quia robore ChristumPM Edocuit, stabilis qui solet esse petra.EA Testis erat vivus, sed nunc monumenta loquunturTR Religio verae quid pietatis habet.RT Urna viri cineres tenet haec, colit aetheris ἄσυ[?]VY Spiritus, illustris vivet in orbe labor.SR
main_text.head: JOANNIS HALLERI.
main_text.p: Quàm bene Nasonis cecinit doctissima Musa Conveniunt fatis nomina saepe suis. Sic ego dum Martyr dicor me Christus Jesus Aeterni verbi Martyra constituit. Italus audivit, Gallus, Germanus & Anglus, Martyrium sanctum quod tibi Christe dedi. Illud & absolvi Tigurina doctor in urbe, Hic mea membra jacent, spiritus astra tenet.
main_text.head: VVOLFGANGI HAL-leri Διαλογισμός.
Μαρτυρόφιλῳ & Martyri.
main_text.p: Cur moreris Martyr? cur nos ô chare relinquis? Cur filum resecat pallida Parca tibi? Quis subito morbus te nobis eripit, aut quae Tempore tam celeri vis inimica rapit? Profueras multum, sed quid nunc proderis orbi, In gelidam felix corpore versus humum?

page.notes: The Greek word in the acrostic verse (colit aetheris ...) is hard to read; read as ἄσυ[?]. The Greek title Μαρτυρόφιλῳ is a best reading of a small, worn line. The left and right acrostic letters are marginal notes beside the verse lines. The signature M 3 is at the foot right. Spelling u/v and i/j normalised per rules; the printed "VVOLFGANGI" is kept as printed.
